title: The iu8 sparse exact repair pass costs 4808 ms and does not respond to the risk multiplier
verdict: the repair time is flat across a 3.40x change in repaired-row share; the mechanism is NOT a fixed over-launched grid (an earlier reading of this trace was a units error - see correction)
quant: mixed GGUF: Q4_K gate/up experts, Q5_1 down experts, Q5_K 2 tensors, Q8_0 5 tensors

host.note: not the gfx1100/W7900 default hardware; absolute rates are not comparable to W7900 rows

instrument.jit: warmed outside the profiler; --require-cached-build plus a precomputed compiler-version file, so no hipcc ran under the profiler
instrument.duration_derivation: End_Timestamp - Start_Timestamp (the CSV carries no duration column); nanoseconds
instrument.grid_units: Grid_Size_X/Y/Z are TOTAL WORK-ITEMS, not blocks. Workgroup_Size_X is the block size. Divide to get the block count.

command: HIPENGINE_QWEN4_EXP_Q4_IU8_RISK_MULT=<4.0|1.0> rocprofv3 --kernel-trace --output-format csv -d . -o trace -- python3 scripts/qwen4exp_profile_gap.py --model-root /home/lhl/models/gguf/unsloth-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL/UD-Q4_K_XL --mode prefill --case-id code-p4096 --execution-profile production --compiler-version-file /tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version.txt --require-cached-build --output prof-<mult>.json
summary: Summing the repair kernels' own durations across the prefill window at risk multiplier 4.0 and 1.0 gives 4808.702 ms and 4844.580 ms - a 0.7% difference with the tighter multiplier marginally SLOWER. Tightening 4.0 -> 1.0 cuts the repaired row share 3.40x (measured previously), so the repair kernels' time does not track how much they repair. The mechanism is still unexplained: the launch geometry is proportional (a 1024-block grid with a grid-stride loop bounded by min(risk_count, max_risks)), so the flat time is not an over-launched grid.

correction.what_was_wrong: An earlier revision of this artifact reported the repair kernel as dispatching a fixed 131072-block grid and inferred a 128x over-launch. That was a units error: rocprofv3 reports Grid_Size_X as total work-items. The repair's real grid is 1024 blocks x 128 threads = 131072 work-items, exactly the wrapper default and exactly what the source passes to dim3(grid_blocks).
correction.how_it_was_caught: qwen35_moe_wmma_tile_map_kernel is launched with dim3(1) blocks and dim3(512) threads (group_scatter.hip:959-963, threads = next_power_of_two(512)); the same trace reports Grid_Size_X = 512, Workgroup_Size_X = 512. A block count of 1 cannot produce 512, so Grid_Size_X is work-items.
correction.independent_confirmation: scripts/qwen4exp_repair_grid_probe.py launches the registered repair kernel directly under the profiler at a known grid_blocks. grid_blocks=1024 -> 131072 work-items; grid_blocks=8192 -> 1048576 work-items. Both are grid_blocks x 128, matching the source and the 1024-block reading.
correction.what_survives: The flat-time observation itself is unaffected: the repair is 4808.702 ms at 4.0 and 4844.580 ms at 1.0. What does not survive is the claimed mechanism and the 3394 ms launch-geometry prize derived from it.

windows.delta_note: The two arms are 0.45% apart in total kernel time and the tighter multiplier is the slower of the two. No kernel-level effect of the multiplier change is detectable.

gguf_q4_k_selected_dual_wmma_iu8_risk_pr.blocks_note: 10 x 800 blocks at workgroup 128 in X - a row-tile x column-tile shape, flat across multipliers as expected for a kernel that always covers the full padded row space.

open_question: The repair cost is flat across a 3.40x change in repaired-row share, but the grid is proportional and the kernel's loop bound is min(risk_count, max_risks). Either risk_count does not in fact differ 3.40x between the two multipliers in this production path, or the repair's cost is dominated by per-launch work that does not scale with the slot count. risk_count itself has not been measured; the deciding run is scripts/qwen4exp_profile_gap.py with --risk-diagnostics at both multipliers.
limits: One host (gfx1151 APU), one model, one quant, one case (code-p4096), one execution profile.
The profiled run is serialized by rocprofv3, so absolute durations are not wall-clock prefill times; the 4.0-vs-1.0 comparison is valid because both arms are profiled identically.
The 3.40x repaired-row reduction is carried over from the previous iteration's measurement, not re-derived here, and is the assumption the open question turns on.
No correctness gate applies: no arithmetic changed and no default was modified.
source: scripts/qwen4exp_repair_trace_sum.py over /tmp/repair-trace/raw-4.0 and /tmp/repair-trace/raw-1.0; scripts/qwen4exp_repair_grid_probe.py over /tmp/repair-probe-1024 and /tmp/repair-probe-8192
